\documentclass{article}
\usepackage{amsthm,amsmath}
\newtheorem{theorem}{Theorem}[section]
\newtheorem{lemma}[theorem]{Lemma}
\theoremstyle{definition}
\newtheorem{definition}{Definition}
\begin{document}
\section{Preliminaries}
\begin{definition}\label{def:norm}
A norm is a function $\|\cdot\|$ with $\|x\| \ge 0$.
\end{definition}
\begin{lemma}\label{lem:tri}
For all $x,y$, $\|x+y\| \le \|x\| + \|y\|$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
Follows from Cauchy--Schwarz. See Lemma~\ref{lem:tri}.
\end{proof}
\begin{theorem}[Main result]\label{thm:main}
Every finite-dimensional normed space is complete.
\end{theorem}
Theorem~\ref{thm:main} uses Definition~\ref{def:norm}.
\end{document}
